evidence_ref: **A flake found by running a green script six times instead of once.** `verify-phase3.sh` failed **2 runs in 3** — `pod SA is ''`, `pod image ''`, `pod tier label is ''` — always EMPTY reads, never wrong values, and the same full-chain log had it green under phase 6 and red under phase 7. Cause: `p3_force_recreate` returns when the **Deployment's** uid changes, but pod GC is asynchronous, so the pod of the deleted generation is still listed and carries no `deletionTimestamp` to filter on; a `-l app=…` poll returned it, and three separate `.items[0]` reads then re-resolved a list GC was emptying between them. One run read the SA fine and got `''` for image and tier one kubectl call later; one run pinned the pod its **previous** run had created. `verify-phase2.sh` held a byte-identical block and was green on GC timing alone. Fixed with `p3_pod_of_deploy` (Deployment uid → owning ReplicaSet → live Pod, one pinned name). **6/6 clean runs of each, every run resolving a different pod** — the behavioural evidence a lint cannot give.
notes: P8-T8, LSN-025. Third instance in one day of `.items[0]`-after-a-selector being a guess (the first was in P1's own pod read), which is the recurrence bar at which this harness mechanizes rather than fixes again.

evidence_ref: `check_p3_pods_resolved_by_ownership` added to `invariants-gate.py` as the second half of precondition **P3**, registered in `binding.md` and run on every PR via `L0-CHAIN.txt`: no script that calls `p3_force_recreate` may index into `.items[]`. evidence_ref: **The three security failures of the first `verify-phase8.sh` run were all false, and the host was the defect.** `kube-scheduler` and `kube-controller-manager` were in CrashLoopBackOff on both Kind clusters — **31 and 29 restarts** on `dev` — losing leader leases as API calls timed out under memory pressure: Colima sat at its **stock 2 CPU / 2GiB** carrying two control planes. With no scheduler, fixture pods never leave `Pending`, so tenant isolation, the egress default-deny and chaos C2 each reported their property ABSENT. Three properties with no code in common do not regress in one run. Raised to **6 CPU / 8GiB** (7.7Gi allocatable, up from 1.9Gi); both clusters healthy, install state intact — the damage was transient, so `dev` was **not** recreated. New precondition **P10** (`p10_assert_control_plane_healthy`, `binding.md`) asserts the cluster can RUN the experiment before any L2 verdict: `/readyz`, a fresh namespace's `default` ServiceAccount (kube-controller-manager's own output, not a proxy for it), scheduler Ready, and **no control-plane restart inside 900s** — because steps 1-3 all pass against a CrashLoopBackOff probed during its up-swing. **rc 2, could-not-run, never rc 1.** Three defects found in P10 by running it: probe namespaces collided on `$$` (a `$$`+counter fix _also_ collided, since a piped caller runs in a subshell — now server-assigned via `generateName`); nested callers re-probed (memoized 0.600s → 0.006s, positives only); and the managed-control-plane branch returned early past the flap check. Behavioural evidence: **rc 2 on both clusters inside the window, rc 0 on both once it elapsed.**
notes: P8-T8c. LSN-026 is **open**: P10 gates `verify-phase8.sh` only, and the other 15 closure scripts are each runnable alone. `L2_SCOPE_FLOOR` 15 → 16 (verify-phase8.sh joined the closure and the floor only fires _below_ itself). Gate 11/11, L0 13/13.

notes: P8-T8c. **A real defect fell out of this: `reload-images.sh` was a silent no-op.** `reload_agents()` asked `make docker-build-agents` for a build and then looked for `:latest`, but P8-T5 had changed the root Makefile's `TAG ?=` to `src-<sha>` to stop publishing `:latest` — so every tier missed, each printed a soft `(skip … not built for this REPO)`, and the script **exited 0 having loaded nothing**. That is LSN-021's shape (a command is "run" and does nothing) over V-MET-013 (two definition sites for one tag, drifted). It is also the whole reason both gateways sat in `ImagePullBackOff`: the one script whose job is to put those images on the host had been quietly declining to. Fixed with a single `AGENT_TAG` governing both the build and the load, and a hard `return 4` where the skip was. Both gateways now run source-built images, 4/4, zero restarts, both Agent CRs `Ready` — under amd64 emulation on arm64, which the build warns about (`InvalidBaseImagePlatform` on `nousresearch/hermes-agent`) and which has so far cost nothing. One further gap surfaced and was papered locally, not fixed: nothing in `dev/` seeds the `<tier>-agent-secrets` Secret the CRs reference, so the pods went `ImagePullBackOff` → `CreateContainerConfigError` until a random local `API_SERVER_KEY` was created by hand.

evidence_ref: **Five L2 lines failed on the consolidated cluster; four distinct root causes, and every one is an artifact of trading disposable per-campaign Kind clusters for a single long-lived one, where later scripts now inherit admission state earlier scripts left behind.** (1) **Pod-hardening VAP contamination** — `verify-phase7.sh` applies `vap-agent-pod-hardening.yaml` and leaves it bound; the netpol fixtures carry `kube-agents/tier`, which is precisely what that VAP selects on, so they were DENIED at admission. The `kubectl run` output went to `/dev/null`, so an instant denial surfaced 180 s later as "never became Ready" — LSN-021's shape. Mechanized once as `run_tier_fixture_pod` in `dev/lib/agent-fixtures.sh` (hardens the fixture with `--override-type=strategic`, since a plain JSON merge patch replaces the containers list and drops the image kubectl just generated; settles a `Terminating` predecessor; prints the refusal), now called by three suites. (2) **A label that does not exist** — `multi-agent-namespace-l2.sh` selected on `kube-agents/agent=<name>`, which appears nowhere in the operator: pods carry only `app: <agent>-gateway` and `kube-agents/tier`. One assertion failed loudly. The node-placement one **PASSED on two empty strings**, reporting the cross-node case exercised on the strength of having found no pods at all; unreadable nodes are now `bad`. (3) **Dataplane V2 ignores `ipBlock` for pod IPs** — LSN-028, measured rather than inferred. (4) The negatives fixture is *supposed* to be refused — see the V-CMP-003 row.
notes: P8-T8c. Three of the four were invisible on Kind for the same structural reason: a fresh cluster per campaign meant no script ever met another script's admission policy. The fourth was invisible because Calico honours a rule Cilium does not.
